name: Cathedral of Notre-Dame, Former Abbey of Saint-Rémi and Palace of Tau, Reims
description: In the champagne city of Reims, northeastern France, this trio of landmarks centres on a 13th-century Gothic cathedral where French kings were crowned for centuries. Its façade bristles with carved statues, and Clovis was baptised here around 500. Nearby, the Abbey of Saint-Rémi keeps a 9th-century nave and the saint's tomb, while the 17th-century Tau Palace completes the ensemble.
